message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to accept, reject, or counter the trade offer from p1.

I have $305 and three unmortgaged avenues. p1 has $954 and several properties including Connecticut Avenue. They are offering $250 for Oriental Avenue.

p2 has a dark blue monopoly with one house each on Park Place and Boardwalk. p4 owns Mediterranean, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania avenues.

Oriental Avenue is dead as a build because Vermont Avenue belongs to p2 and Connecticut Avenue belongs to p1. I will reject the $250 offer. I need to keep Tennessee and New York avenues. I will not pay p2.

The $250 offer is below my walk-away value of roughly $300. p1 still needs Vermont Avenue from p2 to complete their light blue monopoly, so this trade does not immediately finish it. I am checking Monopoly rent tables to assess the dark blue houses.

I am double-checking the exact rent values for Boardwalk and Park Place. I will not rely on uncertain figures from memory.

p2 has $287 and can only afford one more house on either dark blue property. My $305 cash can survive one rent hit but not both. Oriental Avenue is worth roughly $100 to me as a blocking piece, and about $150 to p1 toward their light blue monopoly.

The $250 offer is a premium of $150 above the $100 purchase price. That would raise my cash to roughly $555, giving me more survival money against p2's dark blue and building capital for orange once I acquire St. James. However, p1 would then try to buy Vermont Avenue from p2.

Light blue is a cheap but fast-building threat. My orange set needs St. James Avenue, which costs $180. With $305 I can barely afford it and have only $125 left, so I cannot build houses yet. With $555 cash I could buy St. James and still have $375 to start building. Orange houses cost $100 each, and three with one house each would generate about $300 in rent. Cash is the immediate survival concern, not p2's dark blue houses.

I will counter the offer instead of accepting. I am considering asking for $325 or $350 cash for Oriental Avenue. The $250 offer is $50 below my walk-away value, and p1 has $954 so they can afford a higher price.

I will counter with $350 cash for Oriental Avenue. I am ready to accept $300 if they refuse. The public message will be firm but not hostile.

p2 can add a second house to either dark blue property for $200. That would raise rent to $600 on Boardwalk or $500 on Park Place. I cannot afford that, so cash is urgent.
